channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Indian Billionaire Taps $700 Million Private Credit for Megha Buyout
item.description: A key shareholder of India’s Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd. is seeking to raise about $700 million from global private credit investors to buy out his uncle’s stake in the company, according to people familiar with the matter, in what would be one of the nation’s biggest deals this year.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Das and Baiju Kalesh

item.title: MSCI Rebalancing Threatens to Turn ‘Messy’ in New Indian Auction
item.description: India’s contentious new closing auction system is about to face its biggest challenge yet as billions of dollars in passive-fund trades flow through it.
item.dc:creator: Savio Shetty and Samie Modak

item.title: Grand Canyon Flash Flood Leaves at Least 15 Missing
item.description: At least 15 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a flash flood in the Grand Canyon, the National Park Service said in a statement on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Gray

item.title: Gold Steadies After Tumbling as Warsh Spurs Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold steadied after falling more than 3% on Friday as US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s pledge to fight inflation lifted bets the US central bank will raise interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Shein Set for Long-Awaited Hong Kong IPO Debut (Correct)
item.description: From a peak valuation of 100 billion dollars to a targeted debut at a fraction of that figure, ultra-fast fashion giant Shein is preparing for a long-awaited public listing. But as regulatory crackdowns close tax loopholes and squeeze profit margins, the digital retailer is being forced to radically remake its business model. Bloomberg’s Minmin Low reports from Hong Kong. (Corrects spelling of the company's name in the headline.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taiwan’s Top Regulator Wants to Wean Taiwan’s Insurers Off US Dollar Dependence
item.description: Peng Jin-lung, a former academic who now runs Taiwan’s powerful financial regulator, is taking aim at a decades-old investment model used by the island’s life insurance firms — one of the biggest pools of insurance capital in the world.
item.dc:creator: Betty Hou and Echo Wong

item.title: Trump’s Iran War Sets Test for Xi and Putin’s Security Club
item.description: President Donald Trump’s intensifying economic campaign against Iran is testing the limits of the security grouping Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have spent years expanding as a counterweight to US power.
item.dc:creator: Colum Murphy, Sudhi Ranjan Sen and Ilya Arkhipov

item.title: Asian Stocks Drop on Hawkish Warsh Tone, Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks dropped and the dollar held its gains after hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh strengthened bets on an interest-rate hike next month. Oil climbed as Middle East tensions intensified.
item.dc:creator: Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 31
item.description: Oil rose as fresh fighting flared up in the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting risks to flows from the Middle East after months of conflict.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Japan’s NYK CEO on Alternative Routes Amid Iran War
item.description: Japanese shipping giant NYK's head Takaya Soga in an exclusive conversation with Bloomberg's Shery Ahn discusses how the company is exploring alternative routes due to the conflict in the Middle East. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Australian Dollar’s Top Forecasters Say Winning Run Likely Over
item.description: The Australian dollar’s two-month rally may be nearing a peak, with some of its top forecasters warning that bets on another central bank interest-rate hike have gone too far.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess

item.title: Bond Investors Wary After Warsh Speech Fuels Rate-Hike Wagers
item.description: Bond investors at firms including ABN AMRO Investment Solutions and Brandywine Global Investment Management are voicing skepticism about mounting speculation that Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is poised to raise interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie, Ye Xie and Michael MacKenzie

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 08/30/2026
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Space Network Co-Founder & COO Ross Hamilton, RUV Iceland Correspondent Ingólfur Sigfússon, ABC News State Department Reporter Shannon Kingston, Heritage Foundation Inst. for National Security & Foreign Policy Victoria Coates, CSIS Director of Economics Program Philip Luck, Illinois Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, Unleash Prosperity Chairman and Co-founder Stephen Moore and “Autokill” Author and Fmr. New York City Transit Commissioner Sam Schwartz. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi Warns Iran War Weakens US in Asia
item.description: Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) says the Iran war is depleting key US munitions and pulling military assets from the Indo Pacific, potentially weakening deterrence against China as concerns over Taiwan grow. While on Bloomberg This Weekend, the Illinois Democrat also criticized the administration’s trade fight with Canada and Venezuela oil policy while calling for more US assistance to Nepal following catastrophic flooding. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How YouTube Filmmakers Are Reshaping Hollywood’s Talent Pipeline
item.description: YouTube creators are turning online audiences into big-screen opportunities, with filmmakers like Alex Kister moving from DIY horror videos to studio deals. As platforms, distributors and FAST services open new paths to money and viewers, the creator boom is also flooding the market with content, making it easier to start but harder to win. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors Bet on a Hair Loss Treatment Boom
item.description: Drugmakers are developing a new generation of hair loss treatments, including lotions, pills and longer-lasting injections, targeting a US market where tens of millions of men and women experience pattern hair loss. Joining Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz on Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg News Equities Reporter Avalon Pernell says some treatments could seek approval and reach the market as soon as 2027, drawing investor interest in companies hoping to tap consumers already willing to spend heavily on hair restoration. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shein’s $100 Billion Valuation Falls to $26 Billion
item.description: Shein is heading toward a Hong Kong listing at a valuation of about $26.5 billion, roughly a quarter of its 2022 peak, after earlier efforts to list in New York and London ran into regulatory hurdles. Bloomberg News Consumer Finance Reporter Lisa Du is on Bloomberg This Weekend with hosts Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz and says the fast-fashion giant is pitching investors on expanding beyond its core brand by acquiring or partnering with other labels, even as geopolitical, regulatory and reputational risks weigh on its growth story. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Venezuela Oil Deal Raises Questions Over US Role
item.description: The Trump administration’s deal giving a US-led venture access to 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil could reshape the countries’ economic relationship, but questions remain over its political durability and whether it will provoke a backlash inside Venezuela. Former Deputy National Secuirty Advisor for Middle East Affairs and the Heritage Foundation's Victoria Coates is on Bloomberg This Weekend and argues the agreement could encourage US investment and restore Venezuela’s energy sector, but says economic development must ultimately be accompanied by political liberalization and self-determination. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Bulls Turn to Exotic Options, Spreads in ‘Orderly’ Rally
item.description: Gold bulls rejuvenated by the Treasury Department’s efforts to keep US borrowing costs in check are turning to exotic options and spreads to bet on higher bullion prices.
item.dc:creator: David Marino, Yvonne Yue Li and Christian Dass
